An initial draft peeked the served projection via the adapter's private, underscore-prefixed _lookup_fact helper -- rejected before sealing as a genuine design smell (reaching into another sealed module's internals rather than its public contract) and replaced with a peek through the adapter's own sealed ProjectionReadPort.read() using a synthetic, deterministic BEST_AVAILABLE system request, so drift detection dogfoods the exact same path a real consumer would use

design: rebuild() reads the canonical snapshot from PostgresC3Service.read() (authoritative), peeks the currently-served projection digest via TypeDBProjectionAdapter.read() BEFORE ever overwriting it, and compares; a mismatch is real drift -- the aggregate is added to an in-memory quarantine set and the live (divergent) projection is left untouched rather than silently repaired; a match (or first-ever projection) calls apply_commit to (re)confirm it and clears any stale quarantine. read_if_healthy() is the negative acceptance criterion made executable: it raises PROJECTION_QUARANTINED before ever delegating to the projection's own read for a quarantined aggregate, regardless of the request's own consistency mode

requirement_results.command: rebuild() reproduces the real canonical commit's digest and watermark in the live projection, verified by a subsequent real EXACT_AT_COMMIT read
rebuilding a never-committed aggregate raises CANONICAL_NOT_FOUND rather than fabricating a projection

residual_risks: The quarantine set is in-memory, scoped to one ProjectionDriftDetector instance -- a restarted process loses quarantine state and would need a fresh rebuild pass to re-detect a still-unrepaired drift before it would again refuse to serve it; this matches every other in-memory retained component this session (IdentityRegistry, MarkingEngine) that holds no durable state of its own beyond what the real backends themselves persist, and a future task adding cross-process quarantine durability would extend this design, not replace it.

Drift detection compares the served payload's digest-of-digest (via the sealed ProjectionReadPort.read()'s own result_digest) against a freshly recomputed expectation, rather than reading TypeDB's raw stored payload directly -- a deliberate choice to dogfood the exact same sealed read path a real consumer uses (so drift detection can never diverge from what is actually being served) rather than a lower-level, potentially inconsistent shortcut.

This detector reconciles one aggregate at a time on demand; a full-projection sweep across every aggregate is a scheduling/orchestration concern layered on top of this primitive, out of this task's own scope.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.

One transient environmental blip occurred during exploratory local test iteration (an early, non-final run of the same 6 tests reported errors); it did not reproduce across 7 subsequent consecutive repeats (including the 4 captured in this evidence's own raw log) and is judged a passing infrastructure hiccup under concurrent local load, consistent with this session's other documented transient findings (e.g. the recurring Fuseki OOM), not a real defect in this task's own code.
